answer: Slow-release staking makes fake identities expensive. A new agent posts a $50 bond before joining. The bond never unlocks at once: it trickles back at $5 per epoch, only while the agent does verified work, so each identity earns its deposit back after ten honest epochs. An attacker needing one thousand fakes must lock $50,000 up front, then babysit every fake through months of real tasks before breaking even. It is like lighting a thousand lanterns before a voyage through a canyon: each flame costs oil and attention, and snuffing them out early wastes it all.
